instrument: International Mathematical Olympiad 2007, official English problem paper (imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/2007/2007_eng.pdf)
instructions: Each problem is worth 7 points. Contestants sat three problems per day over two days, with 4 hours 30 minutes per day.
item_text: In a mathematical competition some competitors are friends. Friendship is always mutual. Call a group of competitors a clique if each two of them are friends. (In particular, any group of fewer than two competitors is a clique.) The number of members of a clique is called its size. Given that, in this competition, the largest size of a clique is even, prove that the competitors can be arranged in two rooms such that the largest size of a clique contained in one room is the same as the largest size of a clique contained in the other room. July 26, 20
